title: Identification with continuous étale cohomology
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\Sh(X_{\Et})^{\mathbf N}$ be the abelian category of
inverse systems $(G_n)_{n\geq1}$ of abelian étale sheaves, and let
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}((G_n))=\Gamma(X_{\Et},\varprojlim_nG_n)=
\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X_{\Et},G_n)$. For an inverse system $(F_{n,\Et})$ with
epimorphic transitions and $F_n=\nu_X^*F_{n,\Et}$,

$$
R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}((F_{n,\Et}))\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_{n,\Et})
\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(X_{\Proet},F_n)\simeq R\Gamma(X_{\Proet},\varprojlim_nF_n).
$$

proof.text: Work in a common larger universe where the sites are small. Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\Et})$ and $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$; its exactness and evaluation are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Here is the small-site realization needed to apply the resolution theorem to this category. On $C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ put $\operatorname{Hom}((U,n),(V,m))=\operatorname{Hom}_C(U,V)$ for $n\le m$, and no arrows otherwise; covers have constant index and are covers in $C=X_{\Et}$. A sheaf $H$ on this site is exactly the tower $H_n(U)=H(U,n)$: the sheaf condition at $(U,n)$ is precisely that for $H_n$, and the arrows $(U,n)\to(U,n+1)$ give its transitions. The inverse construction sends a tower to this formula on objects and composite restriction/transition on arrows. Thus the two categories are identified, with exactness levelwise. Abelian sheaves are equivalently modules over the constant integer ring sheaf: integers act by repeated addition, and locally constant integer sections act locally and glue uniquely [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] on this small ringed tower site to $F_{\bullet,\Et}[0]$. Obtain a bounded-below injective tower resolution $F_{\bullet,\Et}[0]\to I_\bullet^\bullet$. To see explicitly that this gives enough injectives, apply it to any object in degree zero. At the lowest negative degree, the differential is monic since negative cohomology vanishes; it splits by injectivity. Remove that contractible pair and repeat finitely to degree zero. A direct summand is injective (extend into the original object and project), so the remaining degree-zero term is injective and contains the original object. The same argument on the punctual site gives enough injectives for towers of abelian groups.

proof.text: Let $T=\Gamma(X_{\Et},-)^{\operatorname{Tow}}:\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab})$. Its left adjoint sends $(A_n)$ to $(\underline{A_n})$: the levelwise adjunction [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] is natural in $A_n$ and the sheaf, so its bijections restrict to families commuting with transitions. This left adjoint is exact. Indeed constant presheaves preserve short exact sequences objectwise, and their sheafifications are the constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; sheafification is exact [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], and tower exactness is levelwise. Consequently $T$ preserves injective objects by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives]. The limit functor is additive and left exact: it is the kernel of $1-s$ on products, or directly the group of compatible families. Limits of sheaves are sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], so evaluating at the terminal object gives the actual equality $\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}=\lim\circ T$ on objects and maps. No assertion that $\lim$ is exact on the étale site is used.

proof.text: For each $n$, evaluation at $n$ has the exact left adjoint $L_n(G)$ with value $G$ at $m\le n$, identity transitions there, and zero at $m>n$. A map $L_n(G)\to H_\bullet$ is uniquely its map $G\to H_n$, the components below $n$ being its composites with the transitions. Exactness of $L_n$ follows from levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Thus evaluation preserves injectives [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives]. In particular $I_n^\bullet$ is a bounded-below injective resolution of $F_{n,\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], the complex $\Gamma(X_{\Et},I_n^\bullet)$ computes $R\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_{n,\Et})$. Its transition maps are obtained by applying sections to $I_{n+1}^\bullet\to I_n^\bullet$; the naturality of the derived comparison in the cited theorem makes them the derived transitions of $F_{\bullet,\Et}$. Likewise $T(I_\bullet^\bullet)$ computes $RT(F_{\bullet,\Et}[0])$. This specifies a single strict tower model for the notation $(R\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_{n,\Et}))_n$.

proof.text:
The resolution $I_\bullet^\bullet$ computes $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. By step 2, $T(I_\bullet^\bullet)$ is itself a bounded-below complex of injectives in $\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab})$. The same theorem therefore computes $R\lim$ on this complex by its termwise inverse limit. Both sides of the first asserted isomorphism are consequently represented by the identical complex
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}(I_\bullet^\bullet)=\lim_n\Gamma(X_{\Et},I_n^\bullet).$$
To relate this computation to the homotopy-limit notation in the statement, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to the punctual site with integer coefficients. The complex $T(I_\bullet^\bullet)$ is bounded below with injective terms, hence K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so it is its own K-injective tower resolution and the total derived inverse limit of that node is represented by the same complex $\lim_n\Gamma(X_{\Et},I_n^\bullet)$. That node gives it a distinguished Roos triangle on the tower $(\Gamma(X_{\Et},I_n^\bullet))_n$, which is the tower $(R\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_{n,\Et}))_n$ of step 3; transporting the triangle along that isomorphism of towers gives an isomorphic, hence distinguished, triangle, so this complex is a derived limit of $(R\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_{n,\Et}))_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit]. The comparison just constructed is canonical and natural, since the resolution comparisons and uniqueness assertion in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] are natural. This proves the first isomorphism, without using the epimorphic-transition hypothesis.

proof.text:
The comparison geometric morphism is $
u_X:X_{\Proet}	o X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Apply [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$. Its exact inverse image, after forgetting the unique integer action, is exactly inverse image of abelian sheaves and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Hence $F_ ullet=
u_X^*F_{ ullet,\Et}$ is a strict tower, $
u_X^*I_n^ ullet$ represents $F_n$, and every transition of $F_ ullet$ is an epimorphism: the cokernel of its preimage is zero and exact inverse image preserves this cokernel. This also fixes the coefficient identification for applying the comparison theorem; no finite-ring hypothesis is introduced.

Resolve the bounded-below complex of pro-étale towers $
u_X^*I_ ullet^ ullet$ by a bounded-below injective tower complex $J_ ullet^ ullet$, using the tower-site construction of step 1 and [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. Step 3's exact-prefix argument applies to either site, so each $J_n^ ullet$ is termwise injective. There is a strict map of towers of group complexes
$$a_ ullet:\Gamma(X_{\Et},I_ ullet^ ullet)\longrightarrow\Gamma(X_{\Proet},J_ ullet^ ullet):$$
its first arrow to $\Gamma(X_{\Proet},
u_X^*I_ ullet^ ullet)$ is the ordinary comparison adjunction unit followed by sections, and its second arrow is sections of the chosen tower resolution. The unit is natural in transitions, as is the resolution map, so $a_n$ commutes with every transition as a chain map. To see that $a_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism, factor it through the étale site. The direct image $
u_{X,*}$ is right adjoint to the exact inverse image of abelian sheaves [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], so it preserves injectives [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], and $
u_{X,*}J_n^ ullet$ is a bounded-below injective complex computing $R
u_{X,*}
u_X^*F_{n,\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. The chain map $u_n:I_n^ ullet	o
u_{X,*}
u_X^*I_n^ ullet	o
u_{X,*}J_n^ ullet$ (adjunction unit, then direct image of the resolution) represents the derived unit $K	o R
u_{X,*}
u_X^*K$ for $K=F_{n,\Et}[0]$. By [sk-prop-sf-comparison] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ ($K$ is bounded below) this unit is an isomorphism, so $u_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Since $(
u_{X,*}G)(X)=G(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $a_n=\Gamma(X_{\Et},u_n)$. Both ends of $u_n$ are bounded-below complexes of injectives, so by clause (2) and the naturality of $\alpha$ in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] the class of $\Gamma(X_{\Et},u_n)$ is identified with $R\Gamma(X_{\Et},u_n)$, an isomorphism. Thus every $a_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], $a_ ullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism of strict tower complexes.

proof.text: Apply total derived inverse limit on $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$ to the isomorphism represented by $a_\bullet$. This is a functor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], so it gives an isomorphism. Its source evaluates to the tower $(R\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_{n,\Et}))_n$ of step 3, and its target evaluates to $(R\Gamma(X_{\Proet},F_n))_n$ by the injective computations of step 6. For an explicit choice compatible with the triangles in the statement, products of abelian groups are exact [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products], so [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies both total limits naturally with $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_n\Gamma(I_n^\bullet)\to\prod_n\Gamma(I_n^\bullet))[-1]$ and its $J$ analogue. The actual chain maps $a_n$ commute with $s$, giving the map of these cones. The cited natural comparison identifies this cone map with $R\lim(a_\bullet)$, so the second isomorphism respects the specified transitions and is independent of resolutions. This uses functorial strict models, rather than assuming that an arbitrary cone choice in a triangulated category is functorial.

proof.text:
Finally the pro-étale tower $F_\bullet$ has epimorphic transitions by step 5. Apply [det-pe-continuous-cohomology-limit] with $W=X$ (the terminal pro-étale object). It gives
$$R\Gamma(X_{\Proet},\lim_nF_n)\simeq R\lim_nR\Gamma(X_{\Proet},F_n).$$
Here the right side is a derived limit of the tower $(R\Gamma(X_{\Proet},F_n))_n$. The object obtained in step 7 is also a derived limit of this tower: its Roos triangle is on the tower $(\Gamma(X_{\Proet},J_n^\bullet))_n$, which the isomorphisms $\alpha$ of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], natural in the transitions, identify with $(R\Gamma(X_{\Proet},F_n))_n$, and transporting a distinguished triangle along an isomorphism gives a distinguished triangle. Any two derived limits of one tower in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ are isomorphic by clause 1 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] (countable products exist by its clause 2, products of abelian groups being exact). So $R\Gamma(X_{\Proet},\lim_nF_n)$ is isomorphic to the object of step 7. Take this isomorphism for the last arrow displayed in the statement, and compose with steps 4 and 7. Every arrow is the comparison for the original strict system. The epimorphic hypothesis is needed here, not to assert surjectivity on étale global sections or on higher cohomology.
